newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone damages Fiji sugarcane, loss unclear.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone damages Fiji sugarcane, loss unclear.

text.p: Fiji's sugar crop would be affected by damage from cyclone Gavin, but losses were still difficult to accurately assess, Fiji Sugar Corp told Reuters.
Jai Narayan, Fiji Sugar Corp's general manager administration, said the crop had suffered from broken tops and lodging after being flattened by winds.

"It's very difficult to assess the situation at this stage. To put a percentage or quantum of loss at this stage would be very difficult. Cane is a hardy crop too and does show a tendency to recover," he said.
"Certainly the wind action and floods would have had effect. The winds were strong," he said.
Sugar Cane Growers Council chief executive Grish Maharaj said all cane areas seemed to have sustained extensive damage from cyclone Gavin but surveys of damage were continuing.
In most areas cane had been flattened and in worst areas it had been broken or uprooted, he said.
Fiji, which produced 4.3 million tonnes of sugarcane in 1996, before Gavin was looking at a "similar, reasonable" crop of more than four million tonnes for 1997, Narayan said.
The country's raw sugar production in 1996 was 475,000 tonnes, with 1997 production forecast by German industry statistician F.O. Licht at 473,000 tones at the end of January this year.
Fiji's sugar crush normally starts in June and runs to December.
Tropical cyclone Gavin lashed the South Pacific nation of Fiji on Thursday and Friday with winds of up to 130 mph, killing at least two people and damaging scores of houses and electrical facilities.
